objective: Run three bounded discovery experiments that distinguish temporal, global-night, and focal-plane explanations for the published DESI MAIN PROGRAM:NIGHT residual signal.

scope.dataset: DESI DR1 public MAIN repeat-observation RV sample

shared_model.petal_constraint: Unweighted zero mean across supported PETAL cells within each PROGRAM:NIGHT after each granular fit. The value 1.0 is frozen before the primary run; it is deliberately not tuned on the discovery outcome.

experiments.question: Do diagnostic night offsets persist across nearby observing nights, consistent with multi-night calibration states rather than isolated nightly noise?
experiments.primary_data: Five-fold diagnostic PROGRAM:NIGHT offsets, median-aggregated after within-fold and within-program gauge removal.
experiments.primary_metric: Pearson correlation between consecutive observed-night offsets separated by 1 to 7 calendar days, reported by program and on within-program standardized pooled data.
secondary_metrics: maximum absolute CUSUM change point with a max-over-program permutation control
experiments.negative_control: 9999 deterministic permutations of offset values among nights within each program, preserving night sampling and the marginal offset distribution.
experiments.decision_rule: Pass if the pooled within-program-standardized test meets every criterion, or if at least two individual programs meet every criterion.
experiments.failure_interpretation: No evidence that the published night term persists beyond individual nights at the tested 1-to-7-day scale.

experiments.question: Are independently fitted same-night BRIGHT and DARK offsets coherent, indicating a calendar-linked state shared across programs rather than a program-only effect?
experiments.primary_data: Within-program-only pair graphs fitted separately, so cross-program edges cannot induce the tested correlation.
experiments.primary_metric: Symmetric Fisher-z combination of BRIGHT_A versus DARK_B and BRIGHT_B versus DARK_A same-night Pearson correlations, plus the raw-r zero-lag excess over the median calendar-lag correlation at lags -30 through -1 and +1 through +30 days.
experiments.negative_control: 9999 deterministic whole-night permutations of contiguous 14-day calendar blocks within the tested series; the same block mapping is used for both source halves of the shifted program. A 1000-draw 14-day block bootstrap supplies the confidence interval.
experiments.decision_rule: Pass only if the preregistered BRIGHT / DARK pair meets every criterion. BACKUP comparisons are secondary negative-control screens and cannot make E2 pass.
experiments.failure_interpretation: The night-associated signal is not demonstrably shared across independently fitted programs.

experiments.question: After source-disjoint PROGRAM:NIGHT correction, does a nested PROGRAM:NIGHT:PETAL zero point still transfer to held-out sources?
experiments.primary_data: The same quality-approved inter-day pairs used by the baseline audit; PETAL is floor(FIBER / 500) for fibers 0 through 4999 after an all-row equality check against FITS PETAL_LOC.
experiments.primary_metric: Incremental reduction in five-fold holdout raw robust width after adding train-fitted zero-mean PROGRAM:NIGHT:PETAL deviations to the PROGRAM:NIGHT model on an identical supported-row intersection.
secondary_metrics: fraction of the original PROGRAM:NIGHT gain captured by the nested term
experiments.negative_control: Observation-consistent PETAL shuffles within EXPID. Run 19 deterministic controls first and automatically extend to 99 only when the real gain is at least 0.02 km/s and exceeds all first-stage controls.
experiments.decision_rule: Pass only if every listed primary criterion is met; otherwise label suggestive only when the real effect exceeds all controls but misses an effect-size or replication threshold.
experiments.failure_interpretation: No evidence for a transferable PROGRAM:NIGHT:PETAL residual of at least 0.02 km/s on the preregistered common support under the specified regularization. Smaller effects and static PROGRAM:PETAL, exposure-, tile-, or stellar-dependent structure remain untested.

reporting_rules.multiple_testing: Each experiment has one primary family. Program-pair subtests use Holm correction; exploratory secondary slices are labeled exploratory.
reporting_rules.novelty_scope: New within this repository and release bundle only; no claim of global literature novelty without a separate source-backed review.

amendments.reason: Read-only feasibility scouting showed that a global PROGRAM:SPECTROGRAPH term would be less diagnostic than a nested PROGRAM:NIGHT:PETAL term. The primary effect-size threshold was changed before building the pair table or running the strict model.
changes: E1 gained a max-CUSUM secondary metric.
E3 changed from PROGRAM:SPECTROGRAPH to PROGRAM:NIGHT:PETAL.
E3 adopted a predeclared 19-to-99 sequential permutation design.

amendments.reason: A skeptical design review identified mechanical dependence and identifiability risks before any independent program fit or PETAL model was run.
changes: E2 froze BRIGHT / DARK as the only primary pair, raised minimum shared nights from 20 to 100, and added symmetric cross-source-half, zero-lag-excess, and 14-day block-bootstrap gates.
E2 replaced iid night-label shuffles with 9999 deterministic whole-night 14-day block controls.
E3 froze min_pairs_per_label=50, damp=1.0, and a within-PROGRAM:NIGHT zero-mean PETAL-deviation constraint before the primary run.
E3 failure language was narrowed to the tested model and effect-size floor.
